newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel stands tough on East Jerusalem settlement.
newsitem.headline: Israel stands tough on East Jerusalem settlement.

text.p: Israel reaffirmed on Saturday it would keep building a Jewish settlement in East Jerusalem, cementing its stand ahead of a summit between Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak.
"Israel has not offered to stop work on the Har Homa neighbourhood. We are not proposing it," Cabinet Secretary Danny Naveh said.

He was responding to an Israel Television report that Israel intended to offer to suspend work on housing for Jews at the site once basic infrastructure was completed and press ahead with building homes for Arabs in annexed East Jerusalem.

The PLO has demanded Israel scrap the construction of 6,500 homes for Jews on the hilltop Palestinians call Jabal Abu Ghneim before peace talks, suspended when bulldozers broke ground in March, can resume.

"We are aiming to restart negotiations with the Palestinians and ending the crisis in talks with (them) while standing firm on continuing to strengthen (Israel's control) of Jerusalem," Naveh told Israel Television.
"This includes continuing to build on Har Homa but we also have several new ideas about building for Arabs in Jerusalem," he said without elaborating.
Israel said on Thursday it had approved the building of 3,400 houses for Arabs in a village opposite Jabal Abu Ghneim.
In Jordan on Saturday, Mubarak struck a note of caution ahead of the meeting with Netanyahu expected to be held on Tuesday in the Egyptian Red Sea resort of Sharm el-Sheikh.

"I cannot guarantee our effort will succeed 100 percent... the circumstances have got very tough," Mubarak told a news conference with Jordan's King Hussein after brief one-day talks to coordinate positions.
Mubarak said his senior adviser Osama el-Baz would return to Israel on Sunday for a second round of talks to prepare for Tuesday's summit on reviving the peace process.
Mubarak said there was an urgent need to break the impasse but said it was too early to talk of an Egyptian initiative to re-activate Palestinian self-rule talks.
Egypt's Foreign Minister Amr Mousa said on Friday the summit would succeed if Israel agreed to stop building settlements for Jews on land captured in the 1967 Middle East war.
